findings.statement: A bare status token that a test prints with a line end right after its own start is taken as the status without looking at the window, and unittest's real status then stands alone as noise. Probe S03: a printed skip replaces the real skip reason; probe S04: a passing and a skipped test swap outcomes, every count equal, exit 0. The README's reason 'nothing in the file tells the two apart' does not hold: the real status remains as a status-shaped noise line. In the 130 real logs that both revisions read (101,150 starts), no noise line is a status token or ends with one, so a refusal would cost nothing there. No effect expected on MR: with zero skips and zero expected failures in the footer, every such misread changes a count or a listing entry and is refused (probe S05); R1 must and R2 is expected to have zero of each, and the baseline logs hold no such line.
findings.required_change: Recommended, not required: refuse (AMBIGUOUS) when, after a direct status, a noise line before the next runner line is a status token or ends with one, or record such lines in the output so that the freeze's checker can require none; correct the README sentence.

findings.statement: The Progress class docstring still states revision 1's rule ('Exact candidates come first; candidates with different statuses refuse the log'), contradicting the corrected module docstring (:43-46) and plan_direct (:667-692); the disposition asked for the docstring to be corrected. README.md:201 defines different_outcome as 'another outcome not covered above, for example skipped and then error', while line 199 places such an entry in new_not_passing as well.

Repeated IDs: (1) a statement joins the events and subtests of every occurrence, so for an ID that runs more than once it does not fix which occurrence holds which event (probe A14: two distributions both match); (2) a later run of the same ID that starts with a direct FAIL, ERROR or skip is read as a further event of the earlier run, and the log is refused (probe A24), fail-closed; AUTHOR-NOTES section 7 states (2), the README does not and says a twice-run ID keeps both runs. No effect on MR: the retained baseline and main logs repeat no ID, D-18's tests run once, and occurrences is compared.
findings.required_change: Recommended: state both limits in the README, or state events per occurrence.

findings.statement: A statement whose outcome is passed (probe A16) or whose outcome contradicts its own events (probe A23) is accepted. Harmless, since nothing is exempt and a contradictory statement never matches, but the disposition describes an attribution as the test's not-passing record.
findings.required_change: Recommended: refuse a statement whose outcome does not follow from its own events and subtests, or state the rule in the README.

findings.statement: No test pins the undetected remaining case of TR-05 (probes S03, S04), the refusal of a repeated ID (probe A24) or a removed subtest (probe A04). Each behaviour is right or documented, but nothing would show a change.
findings.required_change: Recommended: add tests that pin these behaviours.

observations: reports_different compares report outcomes only; a difference only in two read errors is not listed (probe R01); not reachable in MR, where main's report steps passed with readable reports.

TR-05's stricter rule refuses any window with two candidates, so R1's log would be refused if a test printed a line ending with a status token (for example a word ending in 'ok') between a start and its status; none of the 130 real logs has one; AUTHOR-NOTES Q-8 governs that case as a finding of the tooling.
A statement states first lines only, by design (probe A20).
